cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pubic bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with the opposite pubis at the pubic symphysis; joins the ilium and ischium within the hip bone and contributes to the acetabulum.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Body, superior ramus, inferior ramus, pubic crest, pubic tubercle, pecten pubis and obturator groove.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Pectineus, adductor longus, adductor brevis, gracilis and part of adductor magnus attach to the pubis; rectus abdominis attaches near the pubic crest/symphysis.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Symphyseal surface faces medially; body lies anteriorly; superior ramus lies above the obturator foramen.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sacral vertebrae

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: The fused sacral vertebrae form the sacrum, articulating with L5 superiorly, the ilia laterally and the coccyx inferiorly.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Sacral promontory, alae, anterior and posterior sacral foramina, median sacral crest, auricular surfaces, sacral canal and sacral hiatus.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Piriformis arises from the pelvic surface; gluteus maximus and multifidus attach posteriorly; pelvic floor muscles attach to the lower lateral sacrum.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Broad base superior and apex inferior; smooth concave pelvic surface anterior, rough crested surface posterior.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coccygeal vertebrae

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Form the coccyx and articulate superiorly with the sacrum at the sacrococcygeal joint.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Usually 3–5 small vertebral segments with coccygeal cornua and transverse processes most evident on the first segment.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Coccygeus, levator ani and gluteus maximus attach to the coccyx.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Base faces superiorly toward the sacrum and the apex points inferiorly, usually curving anteriorly.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Labium majus

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms the lateral boundary of the pudendal cleft and protects the more medial external genital structures.

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Paired skin folds containing fat, smooth muscle and connective tissue; homologous to the male scrotum.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Extends from the mons pubis anteriorly toward the perineum posteriorly, lateral to the labium minus.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Anterior parts receive ilioinguinal and genital branch of genitofemoral nerves; posterior parts receive posterior labial branches of pudendal nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Labium minus

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Borders the vestibule and helps protect the urethral and vaginal openings.

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Paired thin, hairless skin folds without substantial subcutaneous fat.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies medial to the labium majus and surrounds the vestibule; anteriorly contributes to the prepuce and frenulum of the clitoris.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Mainly posterior labial branches of pudendal nerve, with anterior contributions from ilioinguinal/genitofemoral territories.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Clitoris

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Erectile sensory organ involved in sexual arousal.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Root, body and glans; paired crura form the root.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Located at the anterior end of the vulva where the labia minora meet.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Branches of the internal pudendal artery, including deep and dorsal arteries of the clitoris.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Somatic sensation mainly via the dorsal nerve of the clitoris; autonomic cavernous fibres regulate erection.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Urethra

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Conducts urine from the urinary bladder to the external urethral orifice.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Short tube passing inferoanteriorly from the bladder neck through the pelvic floor to open in the vestibule.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies anterior to the vagina and is closely related to its anterior wall.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: The short female urethra contributes to a higher risk of ascending urinary tract infection.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Urinary bladder

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stores urine and expels it during micturition.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Apex, body, fundus/base and neck; the internal surface includes the trigone.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies posterior to the pubic symphysis and anterior to the uterus and vagina; the superior surface is related to peritoneum.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Parasympathetic pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2–S4) contract detrusor and promote voiding; sympathetic fibres from T11–L2 favour storage.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Mainly superior vesical arteries, with additional vesical branches from internal iliac derivatives.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ureter

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transports urine from the renal pelvis to the urinary bladder by peristalsis.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends retroperitoneally on psoas, crosses the pelvic brim near the iliac vessels, then runs on the lateral pelvic wall and enters the bladder obliquely.

cards.question: Constrictions
cards.answer: At the pelviureteric junction, where it crosses the iliac vessels/pelvic brim, and at the vesicoureteric junction.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: In the female pelvis, passes inferior to the uterine artery near the lateral fornix of the vagina.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Its relationship to the uterine artery is important during hysterectomy because the ureter may be injured.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vagina

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Fibromuscular canal for intercourse, passage of menstrual flow and childbirth.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Extends from the vaginal vestibule superiorly to surround the cervix.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anterior to rectum and posterior to urethra/bladder; superiorly surrounds cervix to form vaginal fornices.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Upper vagina receives visceral autonomic innervation; lower vagina receives somatic innervation mainly via pudendal nerve.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Vaginal and uterine arteries, with contributions from internal pudendal and middle rectal branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Uterus

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Site of implantation and development of the embryo/fetus; myometrium contracts during labour.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Fundus, body, isthmus and cervix.

cards.question: Position
cards.answer: Normally anteverted relative to the vagina and anteflexed at the junction of body and cervix.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Bladder lies anteriorly and rectum posteriorly; peritoneal reflections form vesicouterine and rectouterine pouches.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Uterine artery from internal iliac artery, with anastomoses to ovarian and vaginal arteries.

cards.question: Lymphatic drainage
cards.answer: Fundus can drain to para-aortic nodes and via round ligament to superficial inguinal nodes; body mainly to external iliac nodes; cervix mainly to internal iliac and sacral nodes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cervix of the uterus

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Inferior cylindrical part of the uterus projecting into the vagina.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Supravaginal and vaginal parts.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Vaginal fornices surround the vaginal part; bladder lies anteriorly and rectum posteriorly.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Site sampled during cervical screening; transformation zone is clinically important in cervical neoplasia.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External os of the uterus (ostium)

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Opening of the cervical canal into the vagina.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: At the inferior end of the cervix within the vaginal part.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Allows passage between the cervical canal and vagina, including menstrual flow and sperm transit.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Uterine tube (Fallopian tube)

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transports the oocyte/early embryo; usual site of fertilisation is the ampulla.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Infundibulum with fimbriae, ampulla, isthmus and intramural/uterine part.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Extends from the uterine horn laterally within the superior free margin of the broad ligament toward the ovary.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Tubal branches of uterine and ovarian arteries.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Common site of ectopic pregnancy, especially the ampulla.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ovary

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Produces oocytes and secretes ovarian hormones including oestrogens and progesterone.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Usually lies on the lateral pelvic wall in the ovarian fossa.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Attached to uterus by ovarian ligament and to lateral pelvic wall by suspensory ligament of ovary; mesovarium attaches it to broad ligament.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Ovarian artery from abdominal aorta, with anastomosis to ovarian branch of uterine artery.

cards.question: Lymphatic drainage
cards.answer: Para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ovarian ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from medial pole of ovary to lateral angle of the uterus, just inferior to the uterine tube.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Helps anchor the ovary to the uterus.

cards.question: Embryology
cards.answer: Derived from the gubernaculum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Round ligament of the uterus

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the uterine horn, passes through the deep inguinal ring and inguinal canal, and ends in connective tissue of the labium majus.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Helps maintain uterine anteversion.

cards.question: Embryology
cards.answer: Derived from the gubernaculum.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Runs within the broad ligament before entering the inguinal canal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Rectum

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stores faeces before defecation.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Begins at the rectosigmoid junction around S3 and follows the sacral curve to the anorectal junction.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies posterior to the uterus and vagina; the rectouterine pouch lies between rectum and uterus.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Superior rectal artery with contributions from middle and inferior rectal arteries.

cards.question: Lymphatic drainage
cards.answer: Upper rectum mainly to pararectal and inferior mesenteric nodes; lower rectum also to internal iliac nodes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External anal sphincter muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Provides voluntary constriction of the anal canal and contributes to faecal continence.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Inferior rectal nerves from pudendal nerve (S2–S4), with contributions from S4.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Encircles the anal canal and attaches anteriorly to the perineal body.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posteriorly attaches to the anococcygeal ligament/body and coccyx region.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Bifurcation of the abdominal aorta, usually at L4.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs inferolaterally toward the sacroiliac joint.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Terminates as external and internal iliac arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Pelvis and lower limb through its terminal branches.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Common iliac veins lie mainly posterior; ureter crosses near the iliac bifurcation.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common iliac vein

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Union of the external and internal iliac veins.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends toward the right side of L5 where the right and left common iliac veins unite.

cards.question: Termination
cards.answer: Right and left common iliac veins form the inferior vena cava.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Pelvis and lower limb.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Common iliac arteries lie anterior; the right common iliac artery crosses anterior to the left common iliac vein.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of the common iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs along the medial border of psoas major toward the inguinal ligament, where it continues as the femoral artery.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac arteries are its principal branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Main arterial route to the lower limb; also supplies lower anterior abdominal wall through branches.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: External iliac vein lies mainly medial; femoral nerve lies lateral and outside the vascular sheath.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External iliac vein

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of the femoral vein proximal to the inguinal ligament.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends along the pelvic brim, generally medial to the external iliac artery.

cards.question: Tributaries
cards.answer: Receives inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac veins.

cards.question: Termination
cards.answer: Joins the internal iliac vein to form the common iliac vein near the sacroiliac joint.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Drains most of the lower limb and part of the lower anterior abdominal wall.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Internal iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of the common iliac artery near the sacroiliac joint.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends into the lesser pelvis and usually divides into anterior and posterior divisions.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Posterior division gives iliolumbar, lateral sacral and superior gluteal arteries; anterior division gives pelvic visceral and perineal branches including uterine, vaginal, obturator, internal pudendal and inferior gluteal arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Pelvic walls and viscera, gluteal region, perineum and parts of the medial thigh.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies anterior to the internal iliac vein; branching pattern is variable.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Internal iliac vein

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Formed by tributaries corresponding broadly to branches of the internal iliac artery and by pelvic venous plexuses.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends from the pelvis posterior/medial to the internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Termination
cards.answer: Joins the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Drains pelvic viscera, pelvic walls, gluteal region and perineum.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Connected to extensive valveless pelvic venous plexuses around pelvic organs.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Peritoneum

cards.question: Definition
cards.answer: Serous membrane lining the abdominopelvic cavity and covering intraperitoneal viscera.

cards.question: Layers
cards.answer: Parietal peritoneum lines the body wall; visceral peritoneum covers organs.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: In the female pelvis, reflects between bladder and uterus to form the vesicouterine pouch and between uterus and rectum to form the rectouterine pouch (pouch of Douglas).

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Parietal peritoneum has somatic innervation and is pain-sensitive; visceral peritoneum carries visceral afferent fibres with autonomic nerves.
